sponges text index | photo index Phylum Porifera Crumbly sponge
Amorphinopsis excavans***Family Halichondriidaeupdated Oct 2016

Where seen? This colourful sponge with a crumbly-looking texture is sometimes seen on our Northern shores. Often seen near Rainbow sponges (Suberites sp.) Features: Encrusting to irregular boulder-shaped sponge 10-15cm, surface rough and irregular. Holes not obvious out of water. On the outside, greyish-green, blue. Those growing in shade said to be yellowish. Bright yellow on the inside.


Punggol, Aug 13


Berlayar Creek, Dec 10Photo shared by Loh Kok Sheng on flickr.

*Species are difficult to positively identify without close examination.
On this website, they are grouped by external features for convenience of display.
